question: What type of natural body chemical is misoprostol designed to copy?
explanation: Misoprostol is manufactured as a synthetic version of prostaglandin E1, which naturally stimulates uterine contractions. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is misoprostol so useful in rural health centers that lack reliable electricity?

options.A: It remains stable at room temperature without strict refrigeration
options.B: It completely replaces the need for any blood transfusion services
options.C: It dissolves completely within seconds in plain cold water
options.D: It can only be given safely by senior medical consultants

explanation: Unlike oxytocin which spoils quickly without a cold chain, misoprostol tolerates ambient heat well, making it ideal for rural settings. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h1)

question: What does misoprostol do to the cervix when helping to start labor?

options.C: Instant closure of the internal os

explanation: Misoprostol breaks down cervical collagen to help the cervix soften, efface, and open up for delivery. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h2)

question: How do uterine contractions stop heavy bleeding after the baby and placenta are born?

options.A: They permanently freeze the clotting factors in the blood
options.B: They force the kidneys to produce more clotting proteins
options.C: They squeeze the open maternal blood vessels shut
options.D: They lower the mother's overall blood pressure instantly

explanation: Contractions act as natural clamps, pressing down on the open blood vessels in the uterus to stop postpartum bleeding. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which way of giving misoprostol gets it into the bloodstream the fastest?
explanation: Dissolving the tablets under the tongue bypasses the liver and allows very fast entry into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h3)

question: A woman is bleeding heavily after childbirth and cannot stop vomiting, so she cannot swallow pills. What alternative way can a midwife give misoprostol?
explanation: The rectal route works very well for postpartum hemorrhage when the patient is vomiting or unable to take medications by mouth. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary obstetric use for misoprostol?

options.A: Prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Lowering high blood glucose levels during pregnancy
options.D: Stopping premature contractions at 24 weeks gestation

explanation: Misoprostol is widely endorsed for preventing and managing excessive bleeding after delivery, especially in low-resource settings. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is misoprostol often used when managing an incomplete miscarriage?

options.A: It assists the uterus in expelling retained tissue without surgery
options.B: It cures underlying bacterial infections in the birth canal
options.C: It permanently prevents any future pregnancies from occurring
options.D: It numbs the pelvic floor muscles to eliminate pain entirely

explanation: Medical management with misoprostol offers a safe, non-surgical option for clearing the uterus after early pregnancy loss. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which patient condition means misoprostol should definitely NOT be used to start labor?

options.A: Previous cesarean section scar on the uterus
options.B: A maternal age greater than thirty-five years
options.C: Mild gestational hypertension without organ damage
options.D: A documented history of mild seasonal allergies

explanation: A scarred uterus from a previous surgery has a high risk of tearing open when exposed to strong prostaglandins like misoprostol. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main danger of giving misoprostol at the same time as other strong contraction-inducing drugs?

options.A: Complete failure of the cervix to ever open up
options.B: Dangerous uterine hyperstimulation and potential rupture
options.C: Severe permanent paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Immediate drop in maternal body temperature to zero

explanation: Combining strong uterine stimulants causes contractions to become too frequent and intense, which can harm both mother and baby. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which mild, harmless side effect often happens shortly after a patient takes misoprostol?

options.B: Complete hair loss on the head

explanation: Temporary shivering and mild chills are common side effects of prostaglandins and usually go away on their own. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h6)

question: A midwife is monitoring a woman whose labor was started with misoprostol. The midwife notices five strong contractions every ten minutes, and the baby's heart rate is dropping. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Give another dose of misoprostol to speed up delivery
options.B: Notify the doctor immediately about uterine hyperstimulation
options.C: Ignore the finding because it is a normal side effect
options.D: Encourage the mother to walk briskly around the ward

explanation: Too many contractions in a short time frame signal hyperstimulation, which can stress the baby and requires prompt medical attention. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T4#BMP213_U1_T4_h6)
